pages.title: Start here: how this workspace runs

text.text: A ten-minute tour of the network in this workspace. Share it with producers, editors, hosts and ad sales.
: each show with genre, cadence, hosts, CPM rate, ad slots per episode, average downloads and sponsor value booked.
: from idea to published, with record and publish dates, guest, length, downloads at seven and thirty days, and ad spots sold.
: who you want, who said yes and when they record.
: the inventory, slot by slot, open, sold, aired or make-good owed.
: who buys, each flight, reads owed and delivered, promo codes and downloads guaranteed.
: each show's numbers from the hosting provider.
Monday: the dashboard. Episodes publishing this week, sold spots due to air, make-goods owed.
Daily: editors move episodes forward; producers book guests.
Thursday: ad sales reviews unsold spots and flights ending soon.
First week of the month: last month's downloads entered for every show.
Every morning: what publishes today, and which spots run in it
Every week: four episodes ahead on each show
Every flight: mid-flight note, proof within five days of the end
Every month: downloads by show, CPM rates reviewed

Producers own shows, guests and the calendar. Editors own the cut, the ad breaks and the upload. Ad sales owns sponsors, deals and inventory. The network head reads downloads, sell-through and renewals.

Ledger Lines recorded "Why ledgers lie" with an accountant guest. The editor placed the mid-roll after the story about a missing invoice, where the conversation paused. The episode went out on schedule with two Tidal Bank spots, and seven days later the producer logged its downloads for the sponsor's report.
Sponsors renew when they get what they paid for and hear about it before they ask. This is how a deal moves from pitch to proof, and how we keep the inventory honest.
. A spot's price is roughly the episode's expected downloads divided by a thousand, times the CPM.
Pitch sponsors that fit the audience. A finance show suits a bank; a storytelling show suits books and home brands.

Long Way Round's cartographer episode went out with the Hollis Hardware pre-roll cut short by an upload error. The spot became a make-good. Ad sales placed it in the mapmaker episode's open pre-roll, told the sponsor that afternoon, and included it in the mid-flight note. Hollis asked about a summer flight the next week.

A lighthouse keeper agreed to talk to Small Rooms but had only a phone signal on the coast. The producer sent a backup recorder by mail, ran a sound check two days before and booked a calm-weather morning. The episode is confirmed with a sold mid-roll waiting for it.
